s: A defense contractor runs Kubernetes on VMware vSphere in a secure site that has no connection to the internet or to AWS. The contractor wants an AWS-supported Kubernetes distribution that matches Amazon EKS, with tooling to create and upgrade clusters on its own infrastructure. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Deploy Amazon EKS Anywhere on vSphere in air-gapped mode, using a local registry mirror for the container images.
Use Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes to join the on-premises servers as worker nodes to an EKS cluster in an AWS Region.
Use Amazon ECS Anywhere to register the vSphere VMs as external instances in an ECS cluster.
Deploy Amazon EKS local clusters on AWS Outposts in the secure site.

w.y: EKS Anywhere runs whole Kubernetes clusters (control plane and workers) on the customer's own infrastructure, including vSphere, bare metal and Nutanix, using EKS Distro. It supports air-gapped environments: artifacts are downloaded once and images are served from a local registry mirror.

o.A: Correct. On-premises control plane, EKS-consistent Kubernetes, works with no connection to AWS.
o.B: Hybrid Nodes keep the control plane in the AWS Region, so the site needs network connectivity to AWS.
o.C: ECS Anywhere is not Kubernetes, and its agents need outbound connectivity to AWS.
o.D: Outposts must be connected to its parent AWS Region through a service link (local clusters tolerate only temporary disconnects), and it replaces the company's vSphere platform with new hardware.
